artifact: AR-1: architect ruling for STUDIO-OBS-013 T0 (guided recording evidence: contract shape, internal callback, clock origin, V20, expiry clock)
author: Aria (@architect)
rulingFor: docs/qa/evidence/STUDIO-OBSERVED-NEXT/s0-plan-refresh.json architectRulingsOwed[AR-1]. It gates C1 (contract lane) and V20 (data lane).
mode: Read-only on source. No product, test, story or contract edits. No Gradle, vitest or contract-tool runs. No git writes. Everything under 'verified' was read from the working tree on 2026-10-13. Anything marked 'inferred' was not executed.
status: RULED. Binding on C1, D (V20), B13, B14 (S3 hunk), R13 and R14. Where it conflicts with s0-plan-refresh.json, this file wins; the conflicts are listed under planCorrections.
summary: R1. result.evidence.video reuses the public VideoEvidence shape exactly: {status, error, expiresAt, partial}. The field is `status`, not `state`, and its vocabulary is VideoStatus (PROCESSING|AVAILABLE|FAILED|UNAVAILABLE|EXPIRED). manifestRef is NOT exposed, and neither is any object key. No videoPath field is added.

R2. actionTimings item = {kind, stepId, admissionId, ordinal, startMs, endMs}, all six required. kind is one of step|action|clarificationWait|prefixReplay; the last two are reserved for OBS-015. Values are integer ms. maxItems is 400 = maxActions 200 + maxSourceSteps 100 (step|prefixReplay) + maxModelProposals 100 (clarificationWait). Timings are non-empty only when video.status is AVAILABLE.

R3. New internal route POST /internal/v2/studio/guided-sessions/{id}/recording-evidence, served by a NEW GuidedSessionEvidenceInternalController and GuidedSessionEvidenceService. The plan's reuse of GuidedSessionService.recordEvidence is REJECTED: the video is finalized only at context close, which happens after the session is terminal, and recordEvidence → internal() → active() refuses terminal sessions. The body carries the bridge identity, recordingId, state (STORED|FAILED|UNAVAILABLE), partial and raw action timings only. It has no text, no keys and no timestamps.

R4. The clock origin is the ADR-002 §11.6 run origin, taken by the existing takeRunOrigin() at guided recording-context readiness, with the same STUDIO_RUNNER_SEEK_ORIGIN_CALIBRATION_MS. It is taken once per session and never re-taken.

R5. V20 gets a dedicated table, studio_guided_session_recordings. Each row is ONE immutable fact per session, inserted once and never updated or deleted. PROCESSING and EXPIRED are never stored; they are derived at read time, as executions already do. The V14 studio_guided_evidence table is not written by OBS-013.

R6. Every time judgement is made on the database clock, inside SQL with clock_timestamp(): recorded_at, expires_at (recorded_at + studio.execution.evidence-retention), the EXPIRED check and the callback acceptance deadline (session expires_at + recording settle grace). No application or runner clock decides expiry or acceptance.
verified: openapi.yaml:3345-3361: VideoStatus enum [PROCESSING, AVAILABLE, FAILED, UNAVAILABLE, EXPIRED]. VideoEvidence requires [status, partial] and has properties status, error (string|null), expiresAt (date-time|null) and partial. The field is `status`. s0-plan-refresh AR-1 calls it `state`, which is wrong.

openapi.yaml:3956-3994: RunnerEvidence.state is [PENDING, STORED, FAILED, UNAVAILABLE]. Projection: PENDING→PROCESSING, STORED→AVAILABLE, FAILED→FAILED, UNAVAILABLE→UNAVAILABLE. EXPIRED is the API's judgement and is never reported. partial is meaningful only with PENDING/STORED (ADR-002 §17.3).

ExecutionSnapshotMapper.java:121-141: EXPIRED is derived at read time (AVAILABLE and expiresAt <= clock). It uses the application Clock.systemUTC(). A persisted AVAILABLE with no readable store is published as UNAVAILABLE with the NO_RECORDING_STORE text (:45-46). RunnerReportProjection.java:262-276 sets expiresAt = now + evidenceRetention only for AVAILABLE, and FAILED gets a fixed API-authored error text.

ExecutionVideoService.java:90-127 runs in this order: authorize through the snapshot read, check evidence state (EXPIRED→410; anything not AVAILABLE→404), derive the key server-side (the persisted video_key column is never read), measure size from the store, then serve the range. ExecutionVideoException codes: VIDEO_UNAVAILABLE, VIDEO_EXPIRED, RANGE_NOT_SATISFIABLE, VIDEO_STORE_UNAVAILABLE.

v3/result.schema.json:132-164: evidence {kind const guidedLedger, ref, video {type null}} and actionTimings {array, maxItems 0} are both REQUIRED. The schema has no `definitions` section today. session-view.schema.json embeds result (oneOf result|null).
GuidedSessionService.java:22-24: TERMINAL = {SUCCEEDED, PUBLICATION_CONFLICT, FAILED, UNKNOWN_OUTCOME, CANCELLED, EXPIRED}. FINALIZING is not terminal.

GuidedSessionService.java:2033-2110: every internal() route calls owner() (fence equality AND a live lease, :2087-2096) and active() (refuses terminal sessions and expired sessions, :2098-2110). recordEvidence (:1353-1385) goes through internal(), so it cannot accept a callback after the session is terminal.

GuidedSessionService.java:118-129 reconcileLateModelUsage is the precedent for post-terminal acceptance: 'terminal/expired authority may be charged but never revived'. It checks fence equality WITHOUT lease liveness and does not call active().

GuidedSessionService.java:2134-2217 stop(): sets the state and sends the runner stop after commit. GuidedSessionService.java:552-570 read(): locks the row, then checkUser + checkCurrent, then result(session) only when terminal. GuidedSessionController.java:59-75: the result route asks the publication projector first. GuidedPublicationResultProjector.java:118-119 hard-codes the same literals.

GuidedSessionRepository.java: transaction(), lock() (an unknown id throws FORBIDDEN_SCOPE 403, :41-43), duplicate() (a different digest under the same key gives IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT 409, :104-118) and command() are all public. GuidedInternalSecurity.requireRole (:67) is package-private.

studio-runner/src/run/browser.ts:525-575 launchGuidedBrowser: one page, and any extra page is closed and treated as lost (so there is exactly one video per session). closeBrowser (:554) closes the context and THEN disposeScratch() removes the whole scratch directory. A recordVideo dir inside scratch would therefore be deleted before upload. The replay recordVideo is at :129-132, and its size comes from the runner config RECORDING_WIDTH/HEIGHT (server/config.ts:318, fallback 1280).

studio-runner/src/run/timeline.ts: takeRunOrigin(source, calibrationOffsetMs) is the only origin-taking site. It reads one monotonic sample and one adjacent wall-clock read, and the calibration comes from STUDIO_RUNNER_SEEK_ORIGIN_CALIBRATION_MS (default 0).
studio-runner/src/guided/transport.ts:145-152: route→definition mapping. Any unknown route is validated as `lifecycle`. runtime.ts:26: the callback route union has 4 members.

contracts/README.md 'Raw JSON and timestamps': guided wire readers reject non-integer numeric lexemes, so the guided bridge cannot carry fractional ms. The README also says every bridge route has 'no automatic POST retry'.
limits.schema.json maxima: maxActions 200, maxSourceSteps 100, maxModelProposals 100, maxSessionSeconds 600.
No guided SSE stream exists. Only sse/ExecutionEventsController emits SSE (grep of studio/** for SseEmitter|text/event-stream).

R1_videoEvidenceShape.decision: Add to result.schema.json `definitions.videoEvidence`: a closed object with properties {status, error, expiresAt, partial}, all four required. Replace evidence.video's `{type:null}` with `{$ref:'#/definitions/videoEvidence'}`, following the S1→S3 sequencing below.

schema.status: enum [PROCESSING, AVAILABLE, FAILED, UNAVAILABLE, EXPIRED]: the VideoStatus vocabulary verbatim, no new value
schema.error: oneOf [null, string minLength 1 maxLength 512]. Always API-authored from a fixed table (below). The runner never supplies text.
schema.expiresAt: oneOf [null, string date-time with the shared UTC profile pattern used by session-view expiresAt]

schemaInvariants_allOf: status ∈ {AVAILABLE, EXPIRED} ⇒ expiresAt is a string. Any other status ⇒ expiresAt null.
partial true ⇒ status ∈ {AVAILABLE, EXPIRED} (ADR-002 §17.3: only an existing recording can be partial).

projectionTable_B13_GuidedEvidenceProjec.session: terminal AND db clock_timestamp() < sessions.expires_at + settleGrace

projectionTable_B13_GuidedEvidenceProjec.error: ExecutionSnapshotMapper.NO_RECORDING_STORE text verbatim (share the constant, do not copy it)
'The runner reported that the recording could not be stored'

R1_videoEvidenceShape.manifestRef: NOT exposed. Object keys (video and manifest) are server-derived, stored only in V20, and never appear in any public body, problem detail or response header. evidence.ref stays the guidedLedger reference (= sessionId), unchanged.
R1_videoEvidenceShape.videoPath: Not added. The route is fixed (`/api/v1/studio/guided-sessions/{sessionId}/video`, operationId getGuidedSessionVideo), and status AVAILABLE is the render condition. Trade-off: the UI builds the path from sessionId instead of reading a field. That is acceptable because the path is a documented public route and the frontend allowlist (F-012B class A) keys on the operationId.
R1_videoEvidenceShape.nullSequencing: S1 (C1): evidence.video = oneOf [null, $ref videoEvidence]. This widening is needed because GuidedSessionService and the projector still emit null until B14's S3 hunk. S3 (same unit as B14's hunk): the C lane TIGHTENS it to `$ref videoEvidence` only (null invalid), following the single-path/no-compat rule for this unreleased Studio. After S3 both projections must always emit an object. contracts.validate('v3/result') in result() is what enforces that the projection is installed.
R1_videoEvidenceShape.resultRouteNote: The result route's HTTP status logic is unchanged: terminal → 200. A terminal result may carry video.status PROCESSING. The client re-polls GET /guided-sessions/{id}/result until status != PROCESSING. C1 adds one sentence saying this to the result operation description.

R2_actionTimings.decision: Add result.schema.json `definitions.actionTiming`, a closed object with properties {kind, stepId, admissionId, ordinal, startMs, endMs}, all six required. actionTimings becomes {type: array, maxItems: 400, items: {$ref '#/definitions/actionTiming'}}.

fields.kind: enum [step, action, clarificationWait, prefixReplay]. clarificationWait and prefixReplay are RESERVED: OBS-015 decides their producer and populates them. OBS-013 code never emits them and refuses them on the callback.
fields.ordinal: oneOf [null, integer 0..2147483647]. The ledger coordinate.ordinal. It lets OBS-008 label 'action n of step' without a join.
fields.endMs: oneOf [null, integer 0..2147483647]. null = no completion was observed (e.g. UNKNOWN_OUTCOME).

schemaInvariants_allOf: kind == action ⇒ admissionId is a string AND ordinal is an integer. Any other kind ⇒ admissionId null AND ordinal null.
Top level of result: evidence.video.status != AVAILABLE (including video null) ⇒ actionTimings maxItems 0.
R2_actionTimings.boundDerivation: Per kind: action ≤ limits.maxActions (max 200); step + prefixReplay ≤ limits.maxSourceSteps (max 100), with each stepId appearing at most once across those two kinds; clarificationWait ≤ limits.maxModelProposals (max 100; every clarification originates from a model proposal). 200+100+100 = 400. The schema constant is 400 because draft-07 cannot reference session limits. The backend also enforces the per-kind caps against the session's own (possibly lower) limits.

semantics.action: startMs = the run-clock reading taken immediately before the runtime invokes the browser effect for that dispatch (after local journal consumption). endMs = the reading when the effect's result is known, taken before the outcome callback is sent. It is null when the outcome is UNKNOWN_OUTCOME. Only dispatched actions (dispatchCount 1) can appear.
semantics.step: Derived by the BACKEND, never sent by the runner: one item per stepId that has ≥1 action item. startMs = min(startMs) over that step's action items. endMs = the endMs of that step's action item with the greatest startMs (null if that value is null). This is selection over readings, not calibration (ADR-002 §11.7 item 1 holds).
semantics.ordering: Sorted by startMs ascending. Ties are broken by kind (prefixReplay, step, clarificationWait, action), then ordinal ascending, then stepId (code-point order). The backend stores the merged, sorted list and serves it verbatim.

R2_actionTimings.rounding: The guided wire forbids fractional lexemes (README 'Raw JSON'), so the runner rounds each reading ONCE with Math.round at serialization. The API never re-rounds, re-bases or shifts (ADR-002 §11.7 items 1-3). The ±0.5 ms is immaterial against the 500 ms seek budget (§6.4). This is the guided-wire application of §4.3: round exactly once, by the component that serializes integers.
R2_actionTimings.scaleGuard: The backend refuses (422 INVALID_CONTRACT) any startMs or endMs greater than session limits.maxSessionSeconds × 1000, and any endMs < startMs. This is the enforcing scale assertion that ADR-002 §11.6 item 4 asks for: it catches a process-origin clock that slipped in.
R2_actionTimings.noText: No item carries labels, observation text, locator values, URLs or runtime values. IDs and integers only (AC-2).

R3_internalCallback.readmeRow: | `recording-evidence` | backend | owning-worker | required | `bridge#/definitions/recordingEvidence` | 202 `bridge#/definitions/recordingEvidence` (echo of the accepted request) |

bridgeDefinition_recordingEvidence.properties: the 10 bridge identity fields exactly as definitions.identity (schemaVersion 3, sessionId, workerId, ownerFence, scopeHash, contextId, contextRevision, sourceRevision, configurationRevision, versions) + recordingId + state + partial + timings
bridgeDefinition_recordingEvidence.recordingId: string pattern ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,256}$. The runner generates it once per session recording (UUID).
bridgeDefinition_recordingEvidence.state: enum [STORED, FAILED, UNAVAILABLE]: RunnerEvidence vocabulary without PENDING, because the callback is sent only once the recording is settled
bridgeDefinition_recordingEvidence.partial: boolean, required. ADR-002 §17.3 meaning: true only when the recorder did not close in an orderly way and the file is still playable.
bridgeDefinition_recordingEvidence.timings: array maxItems 200 (= max maxActions), items $ref result.schema.json#/definitions/actionTiming. Only kind=action is accepted in OBS-013 (backend semantic check). The schema-level item is the shared definition, so OBS-015 needs no bridge change.
allOf: state != STORED ⇒ partial const false AND timings maxItems 0
bridgeDefinition_recordingEvidence.forbidden: no key, no manifest reference, no URL, no timestamp, no error text, no observation text

R3_internalCallback.decisionOnRecordEvidence: REJECTED for this route; the plan's auto-decision is overturned. Reason: the webm is finalized only by BrowserContext.close(), which runs in the runner's stop/teardown path, and that path is triggered after GuidedSessionService.stop() has set a terminal state (:2134-2201). recordEvidence → internal() → active() refuses every terminal session with 409, and owner() also requires a live lease that is no longer renewed after stop. The final acknowledgement would therefore be refused in every successful session. GuidedSessionService.recordEvidence stays unmapped and untouched in OBS-013. Its removal is a residue for the B14/014 owner to place; OBS-013 does not decide it.
acceptancePredicate_GuidedSessionEvidenc: 1. GuidedInternalSecurity role check: owning-worker (B13 widens requireRole from package-private to public, a one-word edit; see stopConditions SC-6).
2. Idempotency-Key required (1..256). The runner uses key = 'rec-' + recordingId for every attempt.
3. Validate the body against bridge#/definitions/recordingEvidence (strict wire reader) → 422 INVALID_CONTRACT.
4. repository.transaction → repository.lock(id). An unknown id → 403 FORBIDDEN_SCOPE (the existing behaviour).
5. repository.duplicate(id, 'recording-evidence', key, digest): same digest → return the stored response (202). Different digest → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

6. Body identity equals the session: sessionId == {id}, scopeHash == document.scopeHash (else 403 FORBIDDEN_SCOPE), versions current (else 422/409 per existing guards). workerId == document.owner.workerId == caller.getName() (else 403 FORBIDDEN_SCOPE). X-Owner-Fence == body.ownerFence == document.owner.fence (else 409 STALE_FENCE). Lease liveness is NOT checked. contextId equals the context materialized for that fence (else 409 STALE_FENCE).

7. Session state is NOT checked: any state, terminal included, is accepted. active() is NOT called. The session document and progress are NOT modified. A recording callback never revives authority (reconcileLateModelUsage precedent :118-129).
8. Acceptance window in SQL: clock_timestamp() < studio_guided_sessions.expires_at + settleGrace, else 409 EXPIRED.
9. A V20 row already exists for the session (a different key) → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The recording fact is write-once.

10. Semantic timing checks (422 INVALID_CONTRACT): every item has kind action; each admissionId exists in studio_guided_actions for this session with dispatchCount 1, and its stepId/ordinal equal the ledger coordinate; no duplicate admissionId; the scaleGuard holds; the items are in the R2 sort order. The set of items may be a SUBSET of the dispatched actions, because a dispatch the runner never received has no reading. Refusing the whole recording for that would destroy honest evidence.

11. Insert the V20 row (state projected: STORED→AVAILABLE, FAILED→FAILED, UNAVAILABLE→UNAVAILABLE; timings = derived step items merged with the action items and sorted). Then repository.command(id, 'recording-evidence', key, digest, echo). Return 202 with the echo.
R3_internalCallback.accessCheck: checkCurrent/checkUser are NOT called on this route. The callback reports a fact from the fenced worker and acts on no one's behalf. Read authorization happens on the public video and result routes. Trade-off: a principal who lost CSI access in the meantime still gets the fact recorded but cannot read it. That is the correct split.
R3_internalCallback.retry: Exception to the README's 'no automatic POST retry', and it must be stated in the README row note: recording-evidence carries no browser effect and is a same-key idempotent fact. The runner (guided/evidence.ts) may resend the byte-identical body under the same key, at most 3 attempts, all inside the settle grace. The other bridge routes keep the rule. The rule exists to prevent repeating uncertain browser work, and this route performs none.
R3_internalCallback.settleGrace: Configured as `studio.guided-authoring.recording.settle-grace`, default PT2M, through a new B13 @ConfigurationProperties record (GuidedRecordingProperties) with the default in the record, so no application.yml edit is needed at S1. B14 may add the documented yml line at S3. It must be ≥ the runner's bounded upload + manifest write + callback attempts. B13 adds a startup check if the runner bound is known server-side; otherwise the runbook records it.

runnerSide.R14: transport.ts:145: add route 'recording-evidence' → definition 'recordingEvidence' (validated as BridgeIdentity for sessionId/fence extraction, which works because the identity fields are present). runtime.ts callback union and RuntimeOptions consumer get +'recording-evidence'. guidedMain.ts composes the recorder and the object-store factory from the existing server/config.ts and application.ts settings.
runnerSide.R13: launchGuidedBrowser adds recordVideo to launchPersistentContext ONLY (size = the runner RECORDING_WIDTH/HEIGHT config, the same source replay uses; dir = a session evidence directory that is NOT inside the Chromium profile and NOT removed by closeBrowser's disposeScratch until the upload attempt finishes. It is removed in every path after that). Order on stop: context.close() → classify with recording.ts evidenceFor/partialFor → upload with evidenceUpload.ts under the server-derivable key (R5 key rule) → write the guided manifest → recording-evidence callback → delete the evidence dir. The stop response to the backend does not wait for upload: teardown = browser gone. A mid-session recorder failure may send the callback early with FAILED/UNAVAILABLE and empty timings.
runnerSide.guidedManifest: Serialized by manifest.ts's redact-twice serializer as a separate body type: {schemaVersion 1, kind 'guidedRecording', sessionId, recordingId, workerId, ownerFence, evidenceState, evidencePartial, videoKey, manifestKey, timings (the same rounded action items), disclosure}. disclosure is a constant string: 'Password fills are rendered as masked dots (password-only rule). A page that later displays a secret in plain text is not protected by this recording.' (AC-5). The backend does not read guided manifests in OBS-013; guided recovery from the manifest is a non-goal and is recorded as such.

R4_clockOrigin.decision: ADR-002 §11.6 applies unchanged. The guided runtime obtains its run clock from takeRunOrigin(systemOriginSource, STUDIO_RUNNER_SEEK_ORIGIN_CALIBRATION_MS) at guided recording-context readiness. That is the instant launchPersistentContext({recordVideo}) has resolved and the single page exists (`context.pages()[0] ?? newPage()`), BEFORE verifyBrowserPreferences, the blank proof or any navigation. Every actionTiming reading is clock.now() from that origin.
rules: One origin per guided session, never re-taken. A lost context ends the session (existing behaviour), so a second origin cannot arise.
The production path cannot run without an injected run clock. No performance.now() default in guided/runtime.ts (§11.6 item 1). Tests inject an OriginSource.
OBS-015 prefix replay on the guided handle MUST stamp with this same session clock. It must never take its own origin.
No origin, offset or calibration constant crosses the wire (§11.2).

R5_V20.decision: Dedicated table, migration backend/src/main/resources/db/migration/V20__guided_session_recording.sql. It lands in the single D unit after V19, in numeric order, and V12–V19 are not edited. V14 studio_guided_evidence is NOT used by OBS-013: it stays as it is, and no OBS-013 code writes it.
ddl_normative: recording_id varchar(256) NOT NULL UNIQUE CHECK (recording_id ~ '^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,256}$'),
state varchar(16) NOT NULL CHECK (state IN ('AVAILABLE','FAILED','UNAVAILABLE')),
recorded_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT clock_timestamp(),
FOREIGN KEY (session_id, scope_hash) REFERENCES studio_guided_sessions (session_id, scope_hash),
CHECK (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > recorded_at),
Trigger: BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE ON studio_guided_session_recordings → RAISE EXCEPTION (immutable fact; same style as V15:301). No exceptions.
No secondary index (lookups are by PK).
notes: The state CHECK is the STORABLE subset of VideoStatus. PROCESSING (no row yet) and EXPIRED (expires_at passed) are read-time derivations, exactly like executions (ExecutionSnapshotMapper:121-141). This replaces the plan's 'state transitions' column design: there are no transitions to store.
Error text is not stored. It is derived from state (R1 table). The plan's error_code column is dropped.
The plan's 'offsets jsonb' column is named `timings` and holds the final sorted public list (derived step items + action items).

INSERT computes recorded_at and expires_at from ONE clock_timestamp() sample, e.g. `WITH t AS (SELECT clock_timestamp() AS now) INSERT … SELECT …, t.now, CASE WHEN ? = 'AVAILABLE' THEN t.now + make_interval(secs => ?) END FROM t`, with retention seconds = StudioExecutionProperties.evidenceRetentionOrDefault() (single source, application.yml:263).

Keys are derived server-side at insert by GuidedRecordingKeys: video `studio/{csiId}/guided/{sessionId}.webm`, manifest `studio/{csiId}/guided/{sessionId}.manifest.json`. csiId comes from document.scope.csiId. Each segment must match ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,256}$, otherwise derivation fails closed: the runner does not upload and reports UNAVAILABLE, and the backend refuses with 422. The read route re-derives the key from the session and never reads the video_key column (ExecutionVideoService precedent). The columns exist for lifecycle and audit. There is no collision with execution keys, because execution identity segments are UUIDs.

Key golden vector: the C lane adds fixtures.json `guidedRecordingKeyVector` ({csiId, sessionId} → {videoKey, manifestKey}). Java (GuidedRecordingKeys) and Node (guided/evidence.ts) each test against it. Two derivations with one shared vector avoid the INT-4 drift (ADR-002 §15.6) without adding a runner-context field.
OBS-014's GuidedObservationPruner does not touch V20: timings carry IDs and integers only, no observation content. Session rows are never deleted, so the FK needs no ON DELETE.
Migration pins: InferenceMigrationLatestIT and the other head pins move to 20 in the D unit (s0-plan-refresh lanes.D).

R6_expiryClock.decision: All judgements happen in SQL on clock_timestamp(): recorded_at, expires_at, EXPIRED (`expires_at <= clock_timestamp()` evaluated in the same SELECT that reads the row) and the callback window (`clock_timestamp() < s.expires_at + settleGrace`). The DatabaseClock class is NOT newly constructed for this path (its Javadoc limits it to the two replay factory methods). The SQL form keeps that limit and saves a round trip.
R6_expiryClock.asymmetry: Execution video expiry is still judged on the application clock (ExecutionSnapshotMapper uses Clock.systemUTC()). OBS-013 does not change it. The guided path uses the DB clock because its acceptance window and its expiry are both judged against DB-written instants (sessions.expires_at, recorded_at). Mixing clocks there would add a skew term. Unifying executions is out of scope; recorded as an observation, not a defect.

publicVideoRoute_C1_and_B13.operation: GET /guided-sessions/{id}/video, operationId getGuidedSessionVideo, tag guided-sessions, x-implemented-by STUDIO-OBS-013, parameters GuidedSessionId + download (boolean, default false)
publicVideoRoute_C1_and_B13.refusalOrder: Session authentication → guided read authorization → evidence state → object store. Authorization is GuidedSessionService.read(user, id, 'session'), the public readGuidedSession path itself, not a re-implementation. So 403 (an unknown id and an unreadable CSI alike) and the authority 503 are byte-identical to readGuidedSession for the same caller and id. Then the R1 projection decides: EXPIRED → 410 VIDEO_EXPIRED; any other non-AVAILABLE → 404 VIDEO_UNAVAILABLE. Then key derivation, metadata/size, Range → 200/206/416, store failure → 503 VIDEO_STORE_UNAVAILABLE.
publicVideoRoute_C1_and_B13.declarations: 401 $ref SessionUnauthorized. 403 is described exactly as on readGuidedSession. C1 extracts 404/410/416 into components.responses {VideoNoEvidence, VideoExpired, VideoRangeNotSatisfiable}, and BOTH getExecutionVideo and getGuidedSessionVideo $ref them (ADR-002 §24.3: route-local copies drift). The 503 stays route-local on each operation; the guided one is oneOf [ErrorResponse (store), PlatformErrorResponse (auth filter), the guided v3 error body (authority unavailable)]. getExecutionVideo's status set does not change.
publicVideoRoute_C1_and_B13.B13_extraction: Extract a key-based server out of ExecutionVideoService (e.g. VideoObjectServer.serve(key, filename|null, rangeHeader, logSubjectId)) covering steps 4-5 and the respond/unreachable helpers. ExecutionVideoService keeps steps 1-3 and calls it. The execution behaviour stays byte-identical. The guided download filename is `guided-session-{sessionId}.webm`. Cache-Control private, no-store and Accept-Ranges bytes as today. Partiality is not consulted.
publicVideoRoute_C1_and_B13.pins: StudioContractTest operation count 38 → 39 (re-read the count at landing; if C2a landed first, quote the actual old/new), plus the expected-map row `GET /guided-sessions/{id}/video` = 200,206,401,403,404,410,416,503. confinement.test.ts BASE_SHA256 re-anchored from `shasum -a 256` of the final document, never transcribed. Old and new values are quoted in the story.

backend_GuidedSessionEvidenceTest_and_Gu: The callback on a TERMINAL session within the window is accepted (202) and the session document/progress are byte-unchanged (no revival; state, owner and lease untouched).
The callback after expires_at + settleGrace on the DB clock is 409 EXPIRED. The test moves time with DB-side expires_at, not an application clock fake.

Wrong worker subject → 403 FORBIDDEN_SCOPE. Wrong fence → 409 STALE_FENCE. Wrong scopeHash → 403. Wrong contextId → 409 STALE_FENCE. Unknown session → 403 FORBIDDEN_SCOPE. Role backend-controller → refused.
Same key + same body → 202 with the identical stored echo and exactly one V20 row. Same key + different body → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. New key after a row exists → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

An admissionId not in this session's ledger, an ADMITTED/REVOKED (dispatchCount 0) action, a mismatched stepId/ordinal, a duplicate admissionId, unsorted items, endMs < startMs, startMs > maxSessionSeconds×1000, or kind step/clarificationWait/prefixReplay in the body → each 422 INVALID_CONTRACT with no row written.

Projection: each R1 table row is produced, including the PROCESSING→UNAVAILABLE flip after the deadline with no row, AVAILABLE→EXPIRED on the DB clock, and servesRecordings=false → UNAVAILABLE + NO_RECORDING_STORE.
No public body, header or log line at INFO or above contains video_key, manifest_key, a bucket or an endpoint (the existing AC-6 style sweep extended to the guided route and the result).

Video route: a caller who cannot read the session gets a 403 byte-identical to readGuidedSession. Unknown id → the same 403. PROCESSING/FAILED/UNAVAILABLE → 404 VIDEO_UNAVAILABLE. EXPIRED → 410. Bad range → 416 with the measured size. Store down → 503 VIDEO_STORE_UNAVAILABLE.
ExecutionVideoContractTest, ExecutionVideoEvidenceIT and ExecutionVideoAuthorizationIT stay green with NO assertion weakened (additions only).
After S3: a result built while no projection is installed fails validation, which proves the projection must be wired.
runner_R13_R14: A process-origin clock injected into the guided runtime makes the first action's startMs fail the scale assertion (it must be near 0 relative to readiness, not near process uptime).
transport: route 'recording-evidence' validates against recordingEvidence, NOT lifecycle (a lifecycle body sent on that route is rejected locally).
The evidence dir survives closeBrowser until upload, then is removed on success, failure and kill paths alike.

A recorder failure mid-session gives state UNAVAILABLE (unplayable/no file) and an upload failure gives state FAILED. The two are asserted separately; AC-6's 'recording failure → UNAVAILABLE' case must inject a recorder-side fault, not a store fault.
The serialized callback body and guided manifest contain zero canary hits and no string outside the ID patterns. noRunnerSinks static test unchanged. confinement.test.ts unchanged except BASE_SHA256.

planCorrections: recordEvidence reuse + transactional hook: withdrawn (R3.decisionOnRecordEvidence). The B14 recordEvidence hook hunk is removed from the S3 cross-hunk list. B14's S3 hunk is installEvidence + 2 literal sites.
V20 'state transitions, expiry, offsets': replaced by an immutable single-insert fact. PROCESSING/EXPIRED are derived. No error_code column. Error text comes from state.
V20 state CHECK: the storable subset {AVAILABLE, FAILED, UNAVAILABLE}, not the full VideoStatus set.
maxItems 400 is kept numerically, but it is derived per kind (actions + steps + model proposals), not as maxActions + maxSourceSteps×2.
The bridge timings carry only kind=action. Step items are derived by the backend.
The README route row success is '202 echo of recordingEvidence', not a bare 202. The no-retry rule has a stated exception for this route.
AC-4 'SSE snapshots carry the reference': no guided SSE stream exists (verified). The reference rides the result/session-view reads. Recorded for @po. No story edit is made here.
autoDecisions: [AUTO-DECISION] Keep evidence.video nullable permanently, or tighten after S3? → Tighten at S3 in the same unit as B14's hunk. (reason: Studio is unreleased and single-path/no-compat applies. Trade-off: one extra regen of the bundles; openapi.yaml is not touched, so there is no digest churn.)

[AUTO-DECISION] Who derives step items? → The backend, from the action items. (reason: one producer for the arithmetic and fewer semantic cross-checks. Trade-off: a step whose only action was never received by the runner has no step item.)

[AUTO-DECISION] How the runner learns the object keys → deterministic derivation from csiId + sessionId with a shared golden vector, instead of a new runner-context field. (reason: runner-context is closed and is fed by GuidedMaterializationService, which is outside 013's file set. Trade-off: two implementations, bounded by the vector test.)

[AUTO-DECISION] Store vs derive PROCESSING/EXPIRED → derive. (reason: execution precedent, and an immutable row with no update path. Trade-off: when the callback is lost, PROCESSING can last until session expires_at + grace, up to about 12 min for a session that ended early. Acceptable and honest.)

[AUTO-DECISION] Expiry clock form → SQL clock_timestamp() rather than constructing DatabaseClock. (reason: keeps DatabaseClock's documented two-site limit, one round trip, judged in the statement that reads the row.)

[AUTO-DECISION] Partial subset of dispatched actions accepted → yes. (reason: refusing the whole recording because one dispatch never reached the runner would destroy honest evidence. AC-6 asserts equality on the happy path.)
security: No object key, manifest key, bucket or endpoint on any public surface (result, session-view, video route bodies/headers). The keys are server-derived and the read path re-derives them.
recording-evidence carries only pattern-bounded IDs, integers and enums. There is no free text, so it gives no redaction surface.
Post-terminal acceptance is bounded by owner subject + fence equality + a DB-clock window, and it never mutates session state (no authority revival).
Video reads authorize through the existing readGuidedSession path. There is no new authorization path.
Key segments are validated (^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,256}$), which prevents path traversal into other CSIs' prefixes.
Masked-dots residual (AC-5) is stated in the guided manifest disclosure. The manual inspection stays an OBS-009 gate (C-17).
